June, 1946 penicillin is now becoming widely available, the Blue Angels team makes their first airshow appearance. Kids play freely in the streets and woodlands of the world, a time of bounty and richness for many is upon the world. That world took note of some happenings from this time forward. Small things like odd geometric shapes in grain fields of sophisticated patterns. Odd lights filled the night skies of the globe, primarily around larger cities and their power stations. A year later the world would change.

The month of July 1947 to be exact in a sleepy little desert town near a small dry lakebed used as a small flight school and test ground for American aircraft and pilots. Bright daylight cooked the dry earth a heat shimmering across the horizon. Gusts of wind pick up sand and carry them along the old lake beds scattering the landscape. Glints of light flash high in the sky and flak cannons afar crack to life. Steadily a timer passing the rounds as they pop at high altitude. Plumes of blue white smoke begin to trail behind the glint and it begins to slow in the air.

No sounds come from it as it begins to catch alight its mirror like bodywork showing the green flames in its reflection. Plummeting it begins a shrill whistle of wind as it flows past the opening in the hull, it begins to dive. Only moments before it should have carried on into the ground the craft made a sharp turn and began to skim the landscape at a glide. Lower and lower until it had bled of most of its speed and it dropped out of the air like a stone. Still smoldering a green small flame where it was struck not moments pass when green jeeps appear from seemingly nowhere. Jeeps containing soldiers with rifles, 10 vehicles in total. Each containing 5 soldiers they amass around the downed craft in a circle.

Most can't even make heads or tails of the craft, the others are concerned. Very concerned, in fact. They knew this was big and calls were made to higher ranks immediately. The media was on scene instantly with the army. Sit swarming with reporters for newspapers and radio stations from near and far. Army officials allowed for full disclosure and coverage. Images and reports of the strange craft filled the globe and its airwaves. It was a round disc that had nearly no openings or features other than the round sphere in the middle and the hole blasted in the side. The flames snuffed quickly by the army as quickly as they had arrived.

The next day was the real change. It opened. Splitting along the ring of the disc long spider like legs emerged. Far bigger than what should have fit within the confines of the small craft. With a loud clank the reflective shell fell away, revealing a black rectangular body. Light at its front round and white covered in a mesh of wire to protect the lens.

The world gasped in fear and shock. More came, enough to blot the Sun from the days sky with a menacing reflective flock. Starlings from the stars the radios called them and then the real horror began.

June, 2017: The extraterrestrial leadership has been in power for 70 years.

The fog surrounded the open bridge, gleaming and reflecting the dull street lamps, still burning. A lone figure ran, parting the silver mist with her speed. Her footsteps padded softly and rhythmically, barely echoing in the midnight air. She heard the clanging of the Machine behind her.

20 years had passed since she last saw her parents. They were gallant heroes, standing up to the regime of the totalitarian ETs. They called themselves Tsularian. She called them the enemy.

As it drew closer, she adjusted the mask over her face. After curfew, humans couldn't breathe in free air outside of their solitary pods. But she was The Resistance. Her heart pounded against her chest; each thud resonated through her body as the Machine grew closer. Its light shone, piercing the mist, attempting to find the girl. The resistance called her Blitzen -- after the reindeer. There were eight of them.

Blitzen dashed again, her body moving through the fog, following the shadows. Each step she took would be risky. Blitzen looked down at her knapsack, a glowing blue light emitting from the depths. She covered it quickly. Pressing her trim body against a wall, the light passed by just mere inches from her location. They were close.

The clacking of metal legs on the concrete echoed in the night sky. The Machine grew closer. Blitzen knew it would be only a matter of seconds until it would find her, and she ran.

She held in her sack the end to the regime, and it was up to her to succeed where her parents failed. The clanking and whirring of machines followed close behind her. A lump grew in the girl's throat; her heart beat furiously against her chest again. In a split second, she leapt down an open manhole, to the sewers. Covering it, she ran, the filth and garbage only filtered out by the girl's mask. This time, the resistance would succeed.

The dark sewer held no match for her. Blitzen lifted up a heavy flashlight, gaining her bearings.

Head South, 2 km, west 1 km

She felt the ground shake over her, debris splattering in the liquid soup of human waste. her feet splashed through the waters.

Thank God I remembered to wear my boots

The clamoring above her continued. Finally, it separated from her, heading east. She continued.

At last, Blitzen reached the exit. Climbing up, she briefly dusted herself off. A hidden door -- almost imperceptible, lie just beyond some beat of boxes. She pulled out a key, unlocking it. She shut the door behind her, taking off the heavy gas mask.

"Gentlemen, I have it."
